source.title: Efficient Automated Circuit Discovery in Transformers using Contextual Decomposition
source.authors: Aliyah R. Hsu; Georgia Zhou; Yeshwanth Cherapanamjeri; Yaxuan Huang; A. Odisho; Peter R Carroll; Bin Yu

page_placements.theme: Circuit granularity changes apparent size and reuse

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies CD-T circuit discovery to GPT2-small on IOI and evaluates its head recovery and circuit faithfulness. It also compares circuit-recovery methods and ablation choices, using measures different from the original manual circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own IOI head-relevance findings, faithfulness results, and method comparisons. The cited Wang et al. results and manual circuit are references, not new results from this study. It does not ablate the main name-mover heads to test self-repair, nor report results separated by IOI prompt variant.
record.test_reason: Uses a different circuit-discovery method (CD-T) on GPT-2 small IOI. It measures recovery of the Wang et al. head classes, qualitatively per class and by ROC AUC, against EAP and ACDC. It also compares mean vs zero ablation for IOI faithfulness. These results bear on V4 directly and on V1 (independent recovery of head classes) and V5 (ablation sensitivity) more narrowly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with additions. The authors conclude CD-T recovers manual circuits better than ACDC and EAP (97% average ROC AUC) in seconds. Its circuits beat random circuits and reach faithfulness 1 with fewer nodes than EAP. Agreement with the IOI paper is significant but imperfect, and manual circuits still outperform automated ones of equal size.
record.recipe_differences: CD-T uses analytical contextual decomposition and node-level relevance-based circuit discovery, with mean-activation deviations as the relevant component. It differs from the original study's manual activation/path-patching analysis; the manual circuit is used here as a reference.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares mean and zero ablation for faithfulness; the authors say the IOI curves are quite comparable. It does not report IOI sensitivity results for different metrics or separately evaluated prompt distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: A position-specific CD-T circuit of 0.4% of nodes reaches faithfulness 1 and beats 80% of random circuits up to about 60% of model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finer, position-level IOI circuits much smaller than the head-level circuit can fully reproduce the logit difference.

record.problems: The IOI circuit analysis uses 25 mixed-template examples for discovery and a separate 100 for evaluation. Head-role findings are partly qualitative, the authors report imperfect agreement with the manual analysis, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper notes that relevance scores vary in scale and that the selection heuristic requires tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The cited manual-circuit findings and the model's approximately 99% IOI task accuracy are references or task context, not circuit-intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: Completeness and minimality criteria; causal role verification of each class; faithfulness of the exact 26-head circuit beyond the Figure 2 manual curve.
No ablation of the main name movers to test whether backup heads take over.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints or tasks reusing the IOI components.
Metric choice, prompt-distribution sensitivity, and the partial-explanation question for the original circuit.
No results broken down by name order, template or number of names.

missing.what: Manual (Wang et al.) circuit faithfulness curve, and the statement that manual circuits outperform CD-T and EAP circuits of the same size.
Statement that EAP and ACDC struggle to identify the negative and backup name-mover heads in IOI.
Duplicate-token heads (0,1) and (0,10) drowned out by (3,0).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The faithfulness rows (r5, r6) concern the study's own circuit and were unlinked. The head-class tracing in A.1.1 was guided by Wang et al.'s analysis order, which weakens it as independent evidence. Several key IOI values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports partial agreement with the manual head analysis and circuit faithfulness, but does not establish that the exact 26 heads and seven classes all play their stated causal roles, or test the original completeness and minimality criteria.
Backup name-mover heads are identified as relevant candidates, but the study does not ablate main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.
No IOI circuit comparison across other models, sizes, training checkpoints, or tasks using the same components.
The comparison is based on ROC AUC for recovering a manual circuit; the study does not test equivalence of recovered circuits under other ablation types or metrics.
For IOI, the study compares mean and zero ablation but reports them as comparable. It does not compare metrics or separately evaluate prompt distributions.
IOI circuit discovery uses mixed templates, but no results are reported separately by name order, template, or number of names.

relationships.condition: CD-T on GPT-2 small IOI, node level
relationships.reason: An independent decomposition method recovers most heads of each manual class, including negative and backup name movers (r1-r4). The text reports high ROC AUC, averaging 97% across tasks (r8, figure only).
relationships.display_finding: CD-T recovered most heads in each manual class, including negative and backup name movers; reported ROC AUC averaged 97% across tasks.

source_check.notes: The source contains an unresolved negative-mover identity discrepancy, and its qualitative head tracing partly follows the original analysis. Faithfulness 1 means matching normalized mean logit difference, not demonstrating completeness, minimality or identical behavior on every input.

statements.correction: Analysis negative movers: (10,7), (11,10). Manual-reference negative movers: (10,7), (11,0). Previous-token candidates: (4,11), (2,2). Appendix A.1.1 uses manually guided target positions; IOI-specific AUC is figure-only.
statements.problem: Exact recovery of the reference negative name movers is unresolved: the analysis and reference list disagree on one head. The qualitative tracing also partly follows the original analysis.

statements.correction: GPT2-small; discovery on 25 mixed-template IOI samples; evaluation on another 100; comparable mean- and zero-ablation curves for CD-T circuits obtained under those ablations; no fixed-reference-circuit sensitivity test.
statements.problem: The comparable curves and sample counts are correct, but this does not directly challenge V5 about the reference circuit. A dependence claim also need not imply a difference under every comparison.

statements.correction: Different decomposition method with partial reference-component recovery; qualitative analysis partly guided by Wang et al.; negative-mover identity discrepancy (11,10) versus reference (11,0); comparable mean/zero curves for CD-T-discovered circuits.
statements.problem: The source does not establish exact recovery of both reference negative movers, and comparable CD-T curves are not a direct counterexample for evaluation sensitivity of the reference circuit.

statements.correction: Position-specific IOI circuit: 0.4% of model nodes; more faithful than 80% of random circuits up to around 60% of model size. Separate result: CD-T reaches faithfulness 1 with fewer nodes than EAP; corresponding 0.4% size not stated.
statements.problem: The 0.4% circuit size and random-circuit comparison are supported, but faithfulness 1 is not textually established for that circuit size.
